offence_severity: 7 years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 3000/-
physical_harm: Injuries causing death including laceration of liver, fractured ribs, and internal bleeding
number_of_offences: Charged with multiple offences, but finally upheld for culpable homicide not amounting to murder (Section 304 IPC)
premeditation_planning: Not found; accused did not intend to cause death
key_evidence_accepted: The injuries on the deceased noticed in the post mortem, which were the cause of death, were not described in the Arrest Panchnama, leading to the inference that those injuries were caused to the deceased while in police custody. The deceased was last in the custody of accused No. 1 in the police lock-up about 00.45 a.m. of 17.12.1985, and the burden to prove the injuries was on accused No. 1, which he failed to do.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, PW-21 and PW-22, as credible because they were witnesses to the arrest panchnama and their evidence was used to prove the contents of the arrest panchnama and the entry in the Arrest Register. The court disbelieved the evidence of PW-1, PW-5, PW-6, and PW-7.
post_offence_conduct: Accused Nos. 2 and 3 left the Police Station soon after the arrest, which led to the conclusion that the deceased was not in their custody at the time of death.
trial_duration: Offence: 16.12.1985; Trial judgment: 02.09.1988; High Court decision: 22.03.2007; Supreme Court decision: 19.11.2013
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Not stated; Counsel for the State: Not stated
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed against Subhash, Ananda Bhonsale and Sunil Jadhav; investigation conducted
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal; High Court: Conviction under Sections 302, 342, 218 and 193 r/w s. 34 IPC; Supreme Court: Acquittal of accused Nos. 2 and 3, conviction of accused No. 1 under Section 304 IPC
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was picked up from his house by the accused and that the injuries leading to his death were caused by the accused during custody. They relied on the arrest panchnama and other evidence to establish the accused's responsibility for the deceased's death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the deceased was not picked up from his house but from a Chowk and that the injuries were caused by unknown persons before his arrest. They contended that the accused were not responsible for the fatal injuries as the deceased was not in their custody at the time of death.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that in a prosecution based on circumstantial evidence, the case against the accused must be fully established by ensuring the circumstances are consistent only with the hypothesis of the accused's guilt, conclusive, and exclude all other possibilities.
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda vs. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; State of Rajasthan vs. Kashi Ram (2006) 12 SCC 254; State of M.P. vs. Shyamsunder Trivedi and Ors. (1995) 4 SCC 262
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the accused did not intend to cause death or serious injuries, and the injuries were not likely to cause death. The court found the accused guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304, IPC.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered that the accused did not intend to cause death or serious injuries, and the injuries were not likely to cause death.
other_sentence_order: The court directed that the bail bonds of accused Nos. 2 and 3 shall stand discharged. Accused No.1 was sentenced to seven years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.3,000/-, with further imprisonment of six months in default of payment.
